A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of seven LM–VLM pairs on TaxonomiGQA and TAXOMPS, alongside representational analyses and visual-similarity regressions.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds the authors' property-inheritance evaluation on the Rodriguez et al. dataset in Appendix F and Table 5.

M1.justification: The TaxonomiGQA construction pipeline, model inference procedures, and representational-analysis methods are retained. The new taxonomy appendix documents existing filtering, while the property-inheritance experiment evaluates existing models on another task.

E1.justification: v2 adds property inheritance: projecting novel properties from hypernyms to hyponyms. This substantially extends deployment testing beyond scene-description QA to a taxonomy unrestricted by visual scenes, covering 44 superordinate and 1,281 subordinate categories (Appendix F).

E2.justification: The same seven LM–VLM pairs participate in the retained comparisons and are reused for the new evaluation. InternVL appears only in discussion of concurrent work, not as an additional evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The added evaluation uses 2,016 positive samples, one negative sample per concept, and prompts modified to include the universal quantifier 'all' (Appendix F). These are settings for a new experiment; the original evaluation protocols and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a brief prompt-sensitivity finding: inserting 'all' reportedly improves accuracy, particularly for Qwen2.5-VL-I and MLlama-3.2. No numerical before-and-after breakdown accompanies this observation. Existing controls and representational analyses are retained.

E5.justification: RSA still reports means and standard deviations over 100 sampled submatrices, and existing statistical tests and regression uncertainty reporting are unchanged. Table 5 adds point accuracies without new run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds substantial cross-task evidence: VLMs outperform their LMs in five of seven property-inheritance comparisons, including Molmo-D versus Qwen2 at 0.81 versus 0.60. Existing results remain unchanged. Table 5 identifies MLlama-3.2-I and Llava-OV as exceptions, whereas Appendix F incorrectly names non-instruct MLlama-3.2.

T1.justification: The metric definitions and Equations 1–3 are unchanged, with no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs. Section 5.3 adds conceptual discussion rather than mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claim that VL training improves deployment of taxonomic knowledge without substantially changing that knowledge. The additional evaluation supports this claim without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: New Section 5.3 discusses implications for training-data selection, task-vector transfer, and representational convergence. The limitations newly acknowledge additional text exposure during VL training as a confound and suggest a text-only training control; earlier causal and linear-separability limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly details removal of 52 abstract concepts, inspection of 611 problematic cases, correction of 296, and removal of 315, with a notebook locator. Additional footnotes explain attribute cleaning and the new evaluation prompt. These expand documentation rather than establish changes to the original dataset.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hendel et al. on task vectors and Tan et al. as concurrent taxonomic-evaluation work. It also develops its relationship to the already-cited platonic representation hypothesis. Other bibliography changes largely update existing references.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 5.3 and two appendix sections, refines explanations and tense, and updates affiliations, acknowledgments, and the conference designation. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5 and relocates existing tables and figures through text reflow. Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–4 retain their substantive displays, with limited caption and formatting edits.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the independent property-inheritance evaluation strengthens support beyond TaxonomiGQA, while expanded construction details and the explicit text-training confound improve reproducibility and transparency. The gains are limited: that confound remains uncontrolled, and Appendix F introduces a model-name inconsistency with Table 5.
